text: One existing Raw Titanium + one Coke + 500 mB chlorine -> 1000 mB crude titanium chloride + 250 mB CO2. 240 ticks at 64 JE/t. Default captures CO2 that fits and vents excess; Keep gas stops for full storage. The crude product always needs room.

Existing Chemical Distillation Station: 1000 mB crude chloride -> 750 mB purified chloride + 250 mB spent mineral wash, 240 ticks at 48 JE/t. Empty ethanol/stillage before changing jobs. Process wash in the Mineral Conditioning Station.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

page.title: Titanium Reduction Retort
text: 750 mB purified titanium chloride + two Magnesium Ingots -> one existing clean Titanium Sponge + two Dry Magnesium Chloride. 400 ticks at 96 JE/t includes internal separation and sponge cleanup. Both drawers must fit. Re-electrolyze both salt items to recover two Mg and 500 mB chlorine; it costs power, never generates it.

The existing Arc Furnace melts each sponge into one titanium ingot. Existing titanium tools, armor and components use it. Old titanium recipes remain available. First construction uses steel/copper/ceramics, never its own titanium or magnesium output.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

page.title: Polymer Molding Press
text: Fit one reusable mold in the mold socket; it is locked during a batch and never consumed or worn. All six products take 120 ticks at 32 JE/t. Housings/panels accept existing plastic pellets, PVC resin or new HDPE pellets through an explicit rigid-polymer tag. Fittings require PVC. Insulation, gaskets and hoses require rubber.

Four rigid stock -> one housing or panel; two PVC -> two fittings; two rubber -> three insulation pieces or two existing gaskets; three rubber -> one hose. Housing assembles machine casings; fittings reinforce bronze pipes into steel pipes; insulation assembles copper cable; hoses assemble pipe valves; panels combine with coke into existing carbon-composite building/vehicle panels. These are additional routes, not new gates on old recipes.

Six distinct molds are made from earlier steel plates and simple pattern items. There is no free offcut award: all allocated feed becomes the listed parts. The Polymer Extruder and Clean Polymer Reclaimer add continuous shaping and same-grade offcut recovery. Named ethylene, HDPE, LDPE and staged PVC now connect through the Monomer Preparation Unit and Polymerization Kettle.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

page.title: Monomer Preparation Unit
text: Refinery gas (1000 mB) yields 500 mB named ethylene. Renewable route: 1000 mB bioethanol yields 500 mB ethylene and 250 mB water, with paid dehydration. All process heat is included in JE use; no manual pressure controls.

500 mB ethylene + 500 mB chlorine -> 1000 mB ethylene dichloride; then 1000 mB dichloride -> 500 mB vinyl chloride and 500 mB hydrogen chloride gas. Absorb recovered HCl in the existing Chemical Reactor. Empty incompatible tank contents before switching jobs. Both outlets must fit; nothing is silently vented. Earlier PVC routes remain available.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

page.title: Polymerization Kettle
text: 1000 mB ethylene makes four HDPE or LDPE pellets according to the reusable insert in the protected socket. HDPE uses a catalyst cartridge; LDPE uses its process insert. These select distinct paid processing recipes; they are not consumed. PVC and rubber use existing vinyl chloride and butadiene respectively and need no insert.

HDPE substitutes for ordinary rigid stock in the existing Molding Press, making housings and vehicle panels. LDPE belongs to flexible film, not the rigid-stock tag. The kettle needs only earlier steel, copper and ceramics; HDPE tooling adds existing titanium/magnesium stock.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

page.title: Polymer Extruder
text: Continuous shaping on a supported heated barrel, cooling bed and draw rollers. Install a reusable sheet, film, profile, hose or insulation die. Feed HDPE or existing PVC for sheets, LDPE for film, PVC for profiles, or rubber for hoses/insulation. Tool sockets lock during a batch; automation handles feed and both products through their marked hatches.

Each 160-tick batch at 48 JE/t consumes four stock units. It produces three sheets, films, profiles or insulation pieces, or one hose, plus one matching clean offcut. Both output drawers must have room before work starts. The existing Molding Press keeps its six molds and all prior recipes.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

page.title: Clean Polymer Reclaimer
text: Four same-grade clean offcuts return one stock unit for 120 ticks at 32 JE/t. Three unused LDPE films or PVC profiles also return one matching stock. There is no recipe for mixed trash, other grades, placed blocks or assembled machinery. Recycling pays power and loses material every cycle.

Film wraps cable insulation and cushions machine housings. PVC profiles brace housings and assemble existing colored-plastic blocks. Sheets, insulation and hoses use all their existing recipes. Look up exact construction uses in JEI.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

page.title: From Sand to Silicon
text: The electronics tier turns silicon into chips. It has the cyan look: dark casings, cyan glass and screens, violet conduits.
Pull a silicon boule from 4 silicon and a phosphate in the arc furnace, then saw it into 8 silicon wafers in the sawmill.

page.title: Lithography Station
text: Three wide, two tall and two deep: a cleanroom and an operator's desk with a monitor bank. A silicon wafer, two copper wire and 100 mB of sulfuric acid make four microchips, every 10 seconds at 192 JE/t. Pipe the acid into its tank.
Uses 192 JE/t while working. Holds 60,000 JE.

page.title: Processors
text: Four microchips, an advanced circuit and a gold ingot make a processor in the circuit assembler: the third circuit tier.

page.title: Network Terminal
text: A beige retro computer. Cable it into a power network and right-click it: it shows the network's cables, the rate its slowest cable sets, how many devices it reaches and the energy they hold. It uses no power.

page.title: Control Networks
text: Data cable (optical fibre in a plastic sheath) joins sensors, relays and a logic controller. It carries no power. Channels are the sixteen dye colours: use a dye on a sensor or relay to set its channel.

A sensor goes on a tank, battery, machine or chest and reads how full it is: energy first, then fluids, then items. It gives a redstone signal like a comparator's and reports the exact percentage on its channel. Right-click it to see the reading.
A relay gives a full redstone signal on every side while the controller has its channel on. Set a machine beside it to a redstone mode and the controller runs the machine.

page.title: Logic Controller
text: Runs your factory by rules. Join sensors and relays to it with data cable, then right-click it: each of its eight rules reads "IF channel below or above N% THEN channel ON or OFF". Every second it averages each channel's sensors and works through the rules in order, a later rule overriding an earlier one; a channel no rule switches this time keeps its state, so two rules (off above 90%, on below 50%) leave a dead band. The strip along the bottom shows every channel's reading.

page.title: The Control Room
text: Six control monitor panels in a wall, three wide and two tall, all facing the same way, form one screen. Run a data cable from any panel to a logic controller and it shows every channel: its colour, reading, a bar, a two-minute graph and whether the controller has it on.
An alarm klaxon is switched like a relay: while its channel is on it lights up and sounds.

A control remote flips one channel by hand. Use it on a logic controller to bind it, sneak and use it to pick the channel, and use it to switch. The controller's rules may switch the channel back when their condition next holds. It works within 256 blocks of the controller.

page.title: Rocket Fuel
text: Rockets burn solid propellant: ammonium perchlorate (the oxidizer), aluminum and a rubber binder.

Ammonium perchlorate: a salt and 250 mB of ammonia in the chemical reactor make two. Iodine: eight dried kelp and 100 mB of sulfuric acid make one; with silver dust it makes silver iodide, which seeds clouds.

page.title: Rocket Workshop
text: Builds rockets from up to three ingredients in any slots, like the circuit assembler: solid propellant from ammonium perchlorate, aluminum and rubber; casings, nozzles and guidance units; motors; and the rockets themselves.
Uses 48 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

page.title: Rockets
text: A rocket motor is a casing, a nozzle and two solid propellant. Fire any rocket with right-click under open sky; it rises like a firework and does its work at the top.

Survey rocket (motor, guidance unit, sensor): surveys ores and oil under 7x7 chunks. Cloud-seeding rocket (motor, two silver iodide): five minutes of rain. Clear-sky rocket (motor, two guncotton): five minutes of clear sky. Weather rockets share a two-minute cooldown.

Signal flares (four from propellant, paper and red dye) burst red and tell players within 512 blocks where they went up. Illumination flares (with glowstone) make hostile mobs within 48 blocks glow for 30 seconds.

page.title: Rocket Post
text: A rocket pad sends its cargo to another pad up to 4096 blocks away in the same dimension. Sneak and use a flight plan on the pad to deliver to, then put the plan, a delivery rocket (motor, casing, guidance unit) and up to nine stacks of cargo in the sending pad.
Press Launch, or give the pad a redstone pulse. It needs open sky. The flight takes three seconds plus a second for every 80 blocks; the cargo lands in the target pad's slots.
If nobody is near the target, the rocket waits and lands as soon as that area is loaded again. Hoppers load a pad from the top and sides and unload it from the bottom.

page.title: Ziplines
text: Place two zipline anchors up to 96 blocks apart with nothing solid between them. Stand within 4 blocks of one and use a line-throwing rocket while looking at the other: it strings a steel line.
Use either anchor with an empty hand to ride the line to the other end, hanging below it. A steeper drop is faster. Sneak to let go early (you fall from there).
Breaking either anchor takes the line down. Each anchor holds one line.

page.title: Rocket Launcher
text: The rocket launcher fires a rocket from your inventory (the other hand first), straight and fast. One shot every two seconds.
High-explosive rockets (four from two solid propellant, two guncotton and a rocket casing in the rocket workshop) burst hard where they hit: twelve hearts at the centre, falling off over 5 blocks.
Homing rockets (with a guidance unit instead of the casing) lock on to the hostile mob nearest your crosshair within 48 blocks, if you can see it, and steer into it. Their blast is smaller.
Like grenades, rockets hurt living things only: they never break, move or burn a block.

page.title: Liquid Fuels
text: RP-1 kerosene: hydrocrack heavy fuel oil with hydrogen (in the water tank) over the catalyst in the catalytic cracker. A bucket and 200 mB of hydrogen give 800 mB of kerosene, drawn off with the naphtha. It is jet fuel too: 448 JE/mB in the gas turbine, 480 in the advanced engine.
Liquid oxygen: the cryogenic liquefier condenses a bucket of oxygen into 250 mB.

Fill a rocket casing with a bucket of each in the chemical reactor to make a kerosene tank and a liquid oxygen tank. With two nozzles they make three rocket motors in the rocket workshop, with no solid propellant.

page.title: Booster Rails
text: A booster rail is a straight rail with rocket thrusters. Power it with redstone like a powered rail; unpowered it is an ordinary rail and does not brake.
Load it with solid propellant (use it on the rail, or feed it from a hopper): each gives 8 boosts, up to 64 held.

A cart that rolls on to a powered, loaded booster rail (or stands on it) is kicked to full speed and held there for 10 seconds, up slopes too, trailing flame. A cart standing still goes uphill, or away from a block at one end.

page.title: Machine Sides
text: Every processing machine's screen has six face buttons: front, back, left, right, top and bottom.
Click one to cycle: In (blue), Out (orange), Both (green) or Off (gray).
Eject makes the machine push its results out of its Out faces by itself.
The R button sets how it reacts to redstone: always run, run with a signal, or run without one.

page.title: Brass Item Pipe
text: Joins inventories into a network. Items go to matching sorters first, then take turns between the other inventories.

page.title: Pneumatic Extractor
text: Pulls 16 items every 8 ticks from what it faces and pushes them out of its other sides. A redstone signal pauses it.

page.title: High-Pressure Extractor
text: A steel extractor: 32 items every 4 ticks, four times the brass one.

page.title: Item Sorter
text: Takes only the items in its 9-slot filter, and puts them into the inventory it faces.

page.title: Conveyor
text: Carries items the way you faced when placing it, 2.5 blocks a second, while rotation drives it. A shaft, gearbox or motor on any side drives every conveyor joined to it, for 1 KE per conveyor per tick. Pipes, hoppers and machines load it, and so do items dropped on it; at the end items go into the conveyor or inventory ahead, or onto the ground. It carries you too; sneak to stand still.

page.title: Conveyor Splitter
text: A conveyor that sends items left, straight on and right in turn, skipping any way that is blocked.

page.title: Conveyor Slope
text: Carries items one block up, onto the top of the block in front, or down from a conveyor one block higher behind it. Use it with an empty hand to switch between up and down. It joins and runs with the conveyors around it.

page.title: Brass Wrench
text: Right-click turns a machine. Sneak and right-click to pick a Jugcraft block up, with everything inside.

page.title: Item Crate
text: Holds 32 stacks of one item. Right-click with an item to put it in, with an empty hand to take a stack out (sneak to just look). Works with pipes, hoppers and comparators.

page.title: Capacitor Bank
text: A 2x2 bank of Leyden jars: 4,000,000 JE. It charges from any side and gives power out of the sockets on its front, 4,096 JE/t.
Holds 4,000,000 JE; 4096 JE/t in and out.

page.title: Steel Tank
text: A 2x2 riveted tank: 128 buckets of one fluid. Buckets, pumps and pipes fill and empty it; right-click with an empty hand to read it.
Needs no power.

page.title: Gas Holder
text: A 3x3x3 sphere on legs: 1,024 buckets of one gas, and nothing but gases (liquids go in the steel tank). Pumps and pipes fill and empty it from any face; right-click with an empty hand to read it. Comparators read how full it is.
Needs no power.

page.title: Water Wheel
text: Two blocks tall. The wheel on its right side turns in flowing water: 8 JE/t for each of its two blocks with flowing water beside it, 12 if the water is falling. Still water does not turn it.
Makes up to 24 JE/t. Holds 8,000 JE.

page.title: Cobblestone Generator
text: Makes one cobblestone a second while water and lava touch it, on any sides. Neither is used up. Speed upgrades make it faster.
Uses 4 JE/t while working. Holds 4,000 JE.

page.title: Tree Farm
text: Grows a sapling into six logs in 20 seconds and gives the sapling back, sometimes with an apple, cocoa beans or other extras. Feed the sapling back in with eject and a pipe for endless wood.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

page.title: Crop Harvester
text: Two blocks tall. Harvests the ripe crops in the 9x9 field in front of it, starting the block in front: one crop a second at 24 JE/t. It keeps the drops and plants one of the seeds again, and waits when its three result slots are full. Crops on farmland sit at its own height.
Uses 24 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

page.title: Hydroponic Bay
text: Grows a seed or cutting in nutrient solution under grow lights: no soil, sunlight or farmland, so it works underground, in the Nether or the End. A harvest every 30 seconds uses 100 mB of solution (a fertilizer in a bucket of water, in the chemical reactor) and gives the seed back.
Uses 12 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

page.title: Sprinkler
text: Pipe water in (or use a water bucket) and it sprays the crops within 4 blocks, at its height and one below: every 5 seconds it uses 50 mB and gives each growing crop an extra growth tick. Load up to 16 fertilizer (by hand or hopper) and every 30 seconds it spreads one over the 5x5 crops around it.

page.title: Cotton
text: Sift coarse dirt in the sieve: now and then it turns up cotton seeds (and wheat seeds).
Plant them on farmland like wheat. A ripe plant gives one to three cotton and more seeds; the harvester, sprinkler and fertilizer all work on it.
One cotton spins into one string.

page.title: Speed Upgrade
text: In a machine's upgrade slot: each card makes it faster but uses more energy per item. Four cards: 3x as fast for twice the energy.

page.title: Efficiency Upgrade
text: In a machine's upgrade slot: each card cuts energy use by a fifth. Four cards: 41% of the energy.

page.title: Comparators
text: A comparator next to a generator or battery shows how full it is.
Next to a processing machine, it shows how full its slots are, like a chest.

page.title: The Arcane Concordance
text: The Concordance is the practice of working with the Principles that run through the world. It begins with looking closely. Nothing in this codex teaches by being read: you learn by examining, studying and doing, and the codex records what you have learned.

page.title: Where to Begin
text:
Find something that holds its own light. Amethyst grows in geodes underground; glow lichen and glow berries hang in caves.

Sneak and use a luminous specimen to examine it. Its glow is easiest to judge in darkness: a dark cave, or the open sky at night.

page.title: The Path
text: The Concordance has five stages: Initiate > Practitioner > Adept > Master > Architect. Each opens new practices; no one needs to follow every tradition.

page.title: The Ten Principles
text:
- Radiance: light, revelation and sight
- Ember: heat, combustion and change by fire
- Rime: cold, stillness and preservation
- Tempest: storm, charge and sudden motion
- Strata: stone, structure and weight
- Verdance: growth, life and renewal
- Tide: flow, solution and exchange
- Tether: binding, sympathy and agreements
- Echo: memory, sound, dreams and knowledge
- Hollow: absence, decay and endings

page.title: Resources Are Not Interchangeable
text:
- Focus (personal attention)
- Ley Charge (operational energy)
- Principle Essence (material value)
- Vitae (biological expenditure)
- Astral Resonance (celestial alignment)
- Bound Will (supernatural identity)
- Prima Materia (equivalence value)

Nothing turns one into another except a recipe that names both, with its loss.

page.title: Knowledge
text: Knowledge is not a resource. A research entry moves through four states, Encountered, Observed, Understood and Mastered, from evidence you gather yourself. Repeating the same observation adds nothing.

page.title: Focus
text:
Every invocation spends Focus. You hold at most 20 points; one returns every 2 seconds, whatever you are doing. Focus is yours alone: no item, device or trade can store it.

While you hold an instrument, your Focus shows at the bottom right of the screen.

page.title: Initiate's Wand
text: An instrument channels invocations. Hold it in your main hand; the invocations you have understood appear on the spell bar, and the first is cast with the use key.
Recipe: jugcraft:initiate_wand. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Casting
text: The spell bar lists your invocations in order. The use key casts the first; the number keys 2, 3 and on cast the ones after it. While the instrument is in your hand those number keys cast instead of changing the hotbar slot: scroll to change slot, or bind Spell Engine's own spell keys in Controls to free them.

page.title: Research Notes
text: Use a blank sheet to write down every research entry you have begun, as far as you have come (up to understood). Anyone else can use your notes to read them; reading does not use them up.
Recipe: jugcraft:research_notes. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: What Notes Can Teach
text: Notes are a shared record, not experience. Where an entry accepts notes, reading them can stand in for one way of understanding it, but you must still encounter and observe it yourself, and mastery comes only from your own practice. Notes from the same writer count once, and your own notes teach you nothing new.

page.title: First Light
text:
Some things hold light of their own. Sneak and use one to examine it.

Luminous specimens:
- Amethyst Shard
- Glowstone Dust
- Glowcap
- Glimmerbloom
- Jack-o'-Lantern Mushroom
- Glow Ink Sac
- Glow Lichen
- Glow Berries

page.title: Encountered
text: You have handled a luminous specimen and noticed its glow. Now judge it where there is no other light.

page.title: Observed
text: In darkness (light 4 or less) the glow is the specimen's own. To understand it, study a specimen at a Lampwright's Bench, examine 3 different specimens in darkness, or read Research Notes from someone who has understood it.

page.title: Understood
text:
Radiance can be gathered and set loose. You can now cast Kindle, Dawn Aegis and Revelation with an instrument, and kindle, infuse and channel lanterns at a Lampwright's Bench.

To master First Light, Kindle light in 8 different chunks.

page.title: Mastered
text: You can now cast Lance of Dawn, Flashstep and Lanternward, and every First Light invocation costs less Focus (see Invocations).

page.title: Lampwright's Bench
text: The bench holds one specimen and one piece of work. Its buttons say what they need when they cannot run.
Recipe: jugcraft:lampwright_bench. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Study
text: Study reads a specimen for 5 seconds. The specimen is held while it is read and used up only when the study finishes; cancel, break the bench or take the specimen and nothing is lost. If you are away when it finishes, the bench keeps your notes until you next open it.

page.title: Lanterns
text:
Once First Light is understood: Kindle turns a lantern and an amethyst shard into a Kindled Lantern with 8 Radiance. Infuse adds a specimen's Radiance to a Kindled Lantern, up to 64; a specimen that would overfill it is refused. Channel spends 6 Focus for 2 Radiance.

- Amethyst Shard: 8 Radiance
- Glowstone Dust: 6 Radiance
- Glowcap: 4 Radiance
- Glimmerbloom: 3 Radiance
- Jack-o'-Lantern Mushroom: 3 Radiance
- Glow Ink Sac: 3 Radiance
- Glow Lichen: 2 Radiance
- Glow Berries: 1 Radiance

page.title: Lumen Sconce
text: A brass stand that burns Radiance for a steady light 15: one measure every 60 seconds, up to 64 measures.
Recipe: jugcraft:lumen_sconce. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Pouring and Drawing
text: Use it with a Kindled Lantern to pour up to 16 Radiance in; what does not fit stays in the lantern. Anyone may pour, so a Lampwright can keep a town's lamps lit. Sneak to draw Radiance back into your lantern: only the sconce's owner may. Only Radiance burns in a sconce, and broken, it keeps what it held, less the measure it was burning.

page.title: Kindled Lantern
text:
Use it to light it or put it out. Lit, it burns one Radiance every 20 seconds whether carried or not, and while it is in either hand the air round you is lit (light 12). Put out, it has spent the measure it was burning. It holds up to 64 Radiance.

A lantern can be given or traded; anyone may carry its light, but only someone who understands First Light can recharge it.

page.title: Composing Spells
text: Once First Light is understood you can write spells of your own. A spell is a few words in order: a delivery (how it leaves you), a selection (what it chooses where it lands), one to 3 operations (what it does) and an optional ending. Join a modifier to the word it changes with +, and write then before a second spell that starts where the first landed.

page.title: Writing and Inscribing
text: Hold an instrument and type `/jugcraft concordance compose check` and the spell to see what it does and costs, or exactly why it cannot work. `compose inscribe` writes it on the instrument and it appears on your spell bar; `compose show` reads it back and `compose clear` wipes it.

page.title: Examples
text:
- `touch struck light`: Light where you touch (2 Focus)
- `here struck ward`: Ward yourself (3 Focus)
- `ray struck sear then here creatures dazzle`: Sear what you aim at, then dazzle what stands round it (8 Focus)

page.title: Limits
text:
The Initiate's Wand holds 8 capacity of words. A spell on it reaches at most 6 different targets, does at most 48 work, branches at most 1 time and lasts at most 60 seconds.

A spell costs the Focus of its words (an operation's for every pulse), taken once when it takes effect: a spell that does nothing costs nothing. Its cooldown is half a second and a quarter second for each Focus, and lasts at least as long as it pulses.

page.title: Here
text:
`here`: The spell lands where you stand; after then, where the spell before it landed.

No reach: it lands at once. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 0.

page.title: Touch
text:
`touch`: The spell lands on the first creature or surface within reach.

Reach: 4 blocks. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 0.

page.title: Ray
text:
`ray`: A straight line of light: the spell lands on the first creature or surface it meets.

Reach: 16 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 1.

page.title: Struck
text:
`struck`: Acts on the one thing the delivery reached: the creature, or else the block.

One target. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 0, Focus 0.

page.title: Creatures
text:
`creatures`: Acts on the creatures nearest to where the spell lands. A harmful operation never touches you.

Up to 4 creatures within 3 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

page.title: Spread
text:
`spread`: Acts on the blocks nearest to where the spell lands that the operation can work on (lights keep two blocks apart).

Up to 4 blocks within 3 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

page.title: Allies
text:
`allies`: Acts on you and the members of your party nearest to where the spell lands. Only helpful operations may choose allies.

Up to 4 of you and your party within 4 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

page.title: Light
text:
`light`: Sets a Kindled mote in open air you may build in.

Lasts 32 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

page.title: Reveal
text:
`reveal`: Makes a creature glow, seen through walls. Revealing another player counts as harming them.

Lasts 10 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

page.title: Ward
text:
`ward`: A shell of light that absorbs harm (Absorption).

Absorbs up to 4 damage for 10 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 2, Focus 3.

page.title: Sear
text:
`sear`: Light that burns: arcane damage, credited to you.

4 damage. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 3.

page.title: Dazzle
text:
`dazzle`: Dazzled creatures stumble (Slowness).

Level 1 for 3 seconds. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

page.title: Intensify
text:
`intensify`: Half as strong again (at least one more): joined to an operation.

+50% strength. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

page.title: Prolong
text:
`prolong`: Twice as long: joined to an operation that lasts.

+100% time. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

page.title: Widen
text:
`widen`: Two blocks wider: joined to creatures or spread.

+2 blocks radius. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

page.title: Extend
text:
`extend`: Eight blocks further: joined to touch or ray.

+8 blocks range. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

page.title: Pulse
text:
`pulse`: Acts three times, a second apart, where it first landed. Its operations cost Focus for each time.

3 times, every 1 seconds. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 0.

page.title: Invocations
text: An invocation is a spell someone wrote before you, in the same words you compose with and under the same limits. You learn it from research, not from an item: an instrument only lets you cast what you have learned. Each has one role: damage, defense, movement, support, investigation or utility.

page.title: Tuning
text: An invocation can be tuned with one modifier from the short list it allows, if you could use that modifier yourself. Tuning changes its numbers, never what it does, and costs that modifier's Focus with every cast. Type `/jugcraft concordance tune` with an instrument in hand to see your tunings, `tune <invocation> <modifier>` to set one and `tune <invocation> clear` to remove it.

page.title: Kindle
text:
Sets a mote of steady light in the open block where you look, up to 16 blocks away, for 60 seconds.

Utility. Reach 16 blocks. Light for 60 seconds.

4 Focus (3 once First Light is mastered), cast 0.6 seconds, cooldown 1.5 seconds. Learned when First Light is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Extend: reach 24 blocks (+1 Focus)

Counter. The mote lights only open air you may build in, goes out on its own, and a block placed in its space replaces it.

page.title: Dawn Aegis
text:
Wraps you in a shell of dawn light that absorbs the next blows.

Defense. Absorbs up to 8 damage for 10 seconds.

5 Focus (4 once First Light is mastered), cast 0.4 seconds, cooldown 12 seconds. Learned when First Light is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Prolong: absorbs up to 8 damage for 20 seconds (+1 Focus)
- Intensify: absorbs up to 12 damage for 10 seconds (+2 Focus)

Counter. A burst of damage breaks the shell, it fades after 10 seconds, and the cooldown leaves two seconds bare; it does not stack with itself.

page.title: Revelation
text:
Makes the creatures round you glow, seen through walls.

Investigation. Up to 6 within 6 blocks. Glowing for 10 seconds.

3 Focus (2 once First Light is mastered), cast 0.8 seconds, cooldown 8 seconds. Learned when First Light is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Prolong: glowing for 20 seconds (+1 Focus)

Counter. Milk clears the glow, it reaches only 6 blocks, and it never reveals your party or players you may not harm.

page.title: Lance of Dawn
text:
A narrow beam of light: arcane damage to the first creature it meets, stronger with arcane Spell Power.

Damage. Reach 16 blocks. 5 arcane damage (+0.5 per point of arcane Spell Power).

5 Focus (4 once First Light is mastered), cast 0.5 seconds, cooldown 2 seconds. Learned when First Light is mastered.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Extend: reach 24 blocks (+1 Focus)
- Intensify: 7 arcane damage (+0.5 per point of arcane Spell Power) (+2 Focus)

Counter. It needs a clear line, strikes one target and telegraphs a half-second cast; magic resistance reduces it, though armour and shields do not.

page.title: Flashstep
text:
Carries you a few blocks the way you face, in a flash.

Movement. A push of 1.2 blocks a tick.

4 Focus (3 once First Light is mastered), instant, cooldown 4 seconds. Learned when First Light is mastered.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Intensify: a push of 1.8 blocks a tick (+2 Focus)

Counter. Walls stop it, knockback resistance shortens it, and it cannot be used again for 4 seconds.

page.title: Lanternward
text:
Mends you and the members of your party round you, and wards them with light.

Support. Up to 4 within 4 blocks. Restores 4 health; absorbs up to 4 damage for 10 seconds.

7 Focus (6 once First Light is mastered), cast 1 seconds, cooldown 15 seconds. Learned when First Light is mastered.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Widen: 6 blocks round (+2 Focus)
- Prolong: restores 4 health; absorbs up to 4 damage for 20 seconds (+1 Focus)

Counter. Allies must stand within 4 blocks, only your party is reached, and the one-second cast can be interrupted.

page.title: Hearthspark
text:
A spark that kindles the unlit campfire, candle or candle cake you look at, up to 16 blocks away.

Utility. Reach 16 blocks. Kindles a hearth.

3 Focus (2 once Hearthbinding is mastered), cast 0.5 seconds, cooldown 1.5 seconds. Learned when Hearthbinding is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Extend: reach 24 blocks (+1 Focus)

Counter. It kindles only hearths you could light by hand there, never sets anything else alight, and a waterlogged hearth will not catch.

page.title: Hearthguard
text:
Banks the fire round you: Fire Resistance for 30 seconds.

Defense. Fire Resistance for 30 seconds.

5 Focus (4 once Hearthbinding is mastered), cast 0.6 seconds, cooldown 20 seconds. Learned when Hearthbinding is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Prolong: Fire Resistance for 60 seconds (+1 Focus)

Counter. Milk clears it, it guards against fire and lava only, and the cooldown is long.

page.title: Cinderbolt
text:
A burning shard: fire damage to the first creature it meets, which then smoulders. Stronger with fire Spell Power.

Damage. Reach 16 blocks. 3 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds.

5 Focus (4 once Hearthbinding is mastered), cast 0.5 seconds, cooldown 2 seconds. Learned when Hearthbinding is understood.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Extend: reach 24 blocks (+1 Focus)
- Intensify: 4 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds (+2 Focus)

Counter. It needs a clear line and strikes one target; water, rain and Fire Resistance put out the smoulder, and fire-born creatures shrug it off.

page.title: Hearthflare
text:
A burst of fire round you: fire damage to the nearest creatures, which then smoulder. Never you; stronger with fire Spell Power.

Damage. Up to 4 within 3 blocks. 4 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds.

7 Focus (6 once Hearthbinding is mastered), cast 0.8 seconds, cooldown 10 seconds. Learned when Hearthbinding is mastered.

page.title: Tuning and Counters
text:
Tunings:
- Widen: 5 blocks round (+2 Focus)
- Intensify: 6 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds (+2 Focus)

Counter. It reaches only 3 blocks, the cast can be seen coming, and it spares no one but you: keep allies clear (it never harms players you may not harm).

page.title: Circle Lore
text:
Once you understand First Light, look at things made to hold a shape or a bearing. Sneak and use one to examine it.

Circle specimens:
- Compass
- Lead
- Calcite
- Chiseled Stone Bricks

page.title: Encountered
text: Examine a second, different circle specimen.

page.title: Observed
text: Study a circle specimen at a Lampwright's Bench, or read Research Notes from someone who understands Circle Lore.

page.title: Understood
text:
You can now work rituals: build a Lesser Circle and begin one at its anchor.

To master Circle Lore, complete rituals in 3 different chunks.

page.title: Mastered
text: Your circles hold. Rituals you complete still count for the codex, but mastery asks nothing more of you.

page.title: Circle Anchor
text: A ritual is worked at a Circle Anchor, inside a circle built round it.
Recipe: jugcraft:circle_anchor. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Building It
Reading It
text: Use the anchor with an empty hand to hear what is wrong: a part missing, the wrong block, the space obstructed, a pylon without charge or someone else's, or part of it out of reach (an unloaded chunk). Jade shows the first faults at a glance, and `/jugcraft concordance circle` reads the whole circle.

page.title: Warding Stone
text: Any block in the ritual boundary tag will hold; these are made for it.
Recipe: jugcraft:warding_stone. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Ley Pylon
text: A pylon holds up to 64 Ley Charge, the working energy rituals draw. Each step of a ritual draws from every pylon in the circle at once, all or none.
Recipe: jugcraft:ley_pylon. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Charging
text:
From a Kindled Lantern: use the lantern on the pylon. Every 3 Radiance becomes 2 Ley Charge, up to 15 Radiance a pour; what does not convert stays in the lantern.

From electricity: connect any Jugcraft power source. Every 1000 JE becomes 1 Ley Charge, at up to 64 JE a tick.

Nothing turns Ley Charge back.

page.title: Whose Pylon
text: The pylon belongs to whoever placed it. A ritual draws only from pylons owned by someone taking part (or by no one).

page.title: Beginning
text: Put the offerings in the anchor (use it with each). Then use it with an empty hand: the anchor finds the ritual the offerings answer, checks the circle, and takes your Focus. A ritual for more than one waits 30 seconds for the others, who join the same way. Sneak with an empty hand to take your offerings back before it begins.

page.title: While It Runs
text: Every 2 seconds the ritual checks the whole circle again and draws Ley Charge. Every participant must stay within 4 blocks of the circle's edge. The offerings are held: nothing can be added or taken until it ends. The leader can call it off by sneaking with an empty hand.

page.title: How It Ends
text:
Completed: the offerings are used and the result is made, both at the same moment, once.

Broken off (a part broken, a pylon dry, someone gone, too bright, the anchor's chunk unloaded or the server restarted): nothing is made, the offerings stay in the anchor for you to take back or try again, and the Focus and Ley Charge already spent are gone.

page.title: Containment
text: If a Warding Stone is lost while a ritual runs, the working lashes out: every participant takes its backlash. The offerings are still returned. If the anchor itself is broken, they drop where it stood.

page.title: Adept's Attunement
text:
Attunes an Initiate's Wand into an Adept's Wand, which holds larger spells. What is inscribed and tuned on the wand stays.

Offer: 1 Initiate's Wand, 4 Amethyst Shard, 2 Gold Ingot, 4 Glowstone Dust.
Takes: one practitioner, 6 Focus each, 5 steps (10 seconds), drawing 2 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (40 in all).

page.title: The Adept's Wand
text: An Adept's Wand holds spells of up to 12 capacity, 8 targets and 72 work, with up to 2 branches (the Initiate's Wand: 8, 6, 48 and 1). Take it from the anchor once the ritual completes.

page.title: Lumen Vigil
text:
Two practitioners keep a vigil in the dark: each is shielded, and creatures nearby are outlined.

Offer: 4 Glow Berries.
Takes: 2 practitioners, 4 Focus each, 3 steps (6 seconds), drawing 1 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (12 in all). It must be dark: light 7 or less above the anchor.

page.title: Its Effect
text: Each participant gains 8 points of absorption for 2 minutes, and up to 16 creatures within 16 blocks glow for a minute. It needs two people, but nothing else in the Concordance needs it.

page.title: Alembic Arts
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at what things are made of. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Sugar
- Sweet Berries
- Dried Kelp
- Spider Eye
- Bone Meal
- Honeycomb

page.title: Observed
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: You can now work an Alembic Crucible. To master the Alembic Arts, bottle 3 different outcomes.

page.title: Mastered
text: Your Assay Glass now tells you what a dose would do, and why.

page.title: Alembic Crucible
text: Pour in water (a water bucket is 3 parts; at most 6), then use ingredients on it. Bottle with a glass bottle (a draught) or a bowl (a salve).
Recipe: jugcraft:crucible. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Heat
text:
The crucible takes the heat of what is beneath it: magma 60, a campfire 120, fire 175, lava 220 degrees (nothing: 20). It warms or cools one degree a tick.

Cold below 40 (10% a stir), Warm from 40 (30% a stir), Hot from 90 (55% a stir), Searing from 160 (80% a stir).

page.title: Stirring
text: Ingredients do not dissolve by themselves. Each stir (a Stirring Rod or a stick) dissolves a share of what is still pending, more the hotter it is. But a searing stir keeps only 85% of the dissolved Radiance and Verdance and fouls the mixture.

page.title: Bottling
text: A bottle takes one part's share of everything dissolved: that is its dose. The same process always makes the same mixture, so a good one can be made again.

page.title: Ingredients
text:
- Glowstone Dust: radiance 1.50
- Glow Berries: radiance 0.60, verdance 0.60
- Sweet Berries: verdance 1.00
- Bone Meal: verdance 0.80, hollow 0.30 (contaminant 0.20)
- Sugar: ember 0.90, tide 0.20
- Magma Cream: ember 1.60 (contaminant 0.20)
- Snowball: rime 1.00
- Amethyst Shard: rime 0.80, radiance 0.40
- Dried Kelp: tide 1.20
- Honeycomb: tide 0.60, verdance 0.40
- Spider Eye: hollow 1.20 (contaminant 0.30)
- Sunpetal: radiance 1.00, verdance 0.60
- Dewmoss: tide 1.40, verdance 0.30
- Gloamcap: hollow 0.90, rime 0.40 (contaminant 0.10)
- Mendvetch: verdance 1.40

page.title: What a Dose Does
text:
- Radiance: Night Vision from 0.50 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)
- Verdance: Regeneration from 0.60 a part, 15 s a unit (at most 22.5 s)
- Ember: Fire Resistance from 0.60 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)
- Rime: Resistance from 0.80 a part, 30 s a unit (at most 60 s)
- Tide: Water Breathing from 0.60 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)
- Hollow: Poison from 0.40 a part, 10 s a unit (at most 21.6 s)
- Contaminant: Nausea from 0.50 a part, 8 s a unit (at most 20 s)

A dose below a threshold does nothing for that property; too much contaminant brings nausea.

page.title: Preparation
text: Used as it comes, an ingredient waits to be stirred out. Ground in a Mortar and Pestle it loses a tenth, but most of it dissolves the moment it goes in.

page.title: Sampling Spoon
text: Tells you how hot the mixture is, how much there is, which property is strongest and whether it is murky.
Recipe: jugcraft:sampling_spoon. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Assay Glass
text: Measures every property, dissolved and pending, and the contaminant, a part at a time. Once you have mastered the Alembic Arts it also says what a dose would do and why: which property, how strong against its threshold, and which ingredients put it there.
Recipe: jugcraft:assay_glass. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Formula
text: Use a blank formula on a crucible to write down its whole process (water, every ingredient and how it was prepared, every stir and how hot) while nothing has been drawn from it.
Recipe: jugcraft:formula. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Repeating It
text: Use a written formula on a crucible to set it (sneak with an empty hand to clear it). Fed water through a pipe and ingredients through a hopper (up to 5 kinds waiting), it follows the formula step by step, waiting for the heat each stir needs, and bottles into its output when it has bottles. A Pneumatic Extractor at its side takes the brews out, so the fire can stay beneath. It never guesses: a missing ingredient or the wrong heat simply waits.

page.title: Verdant Husbandry
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at living things. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Moss Block
- Sunflower
- Brown Mushroom
- Lily Pad
- Fern

page.title: Observed
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: Your touch now wakes Verdant Beds and living devices. To master Verdant Husbandry, harvest each of the four crops by hand.

page.title: Mastered
text: You know a garden as well as it knows itself.

page.title: Verdant Bed
text: The Greenwardens' crops grow only in a Verdant Bed, and only once a Greenwarden has woken it (an empty hand wakes it and up to 64 beds joined to it). It holds up to 32 nutrients.
Recipe: jugcraft:verdant_bed. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Five Factors
text:
Moisture (0 to 7): water within four blocks, rain, a wet sprinkler or a canteen keep a bed wet; every step of growth dries it by one.
Light (0 to 15): sun or lamps at the plant, as the server's light has it; never the time of day.
Nutrients: what the bed holds. Growth spends them.
Diversity: the different plants in the 5x5 round it, itself included.
Disturbance: working magic round it.

page.title: Where They Come From
text:
Nutrients come only from declared sources: Mendvetch (fixed from the air), the Mulch Maw (waste, at a loss), bone meal (2 a dose, on a bed or a crop in it) and fertilizer. A broken bed loses what it held.

Disturbance: circle anchor 3, ley pylon 2, crucible 2, verdant heart 2, lumen sconce, lumen mote 1, warding stone 1, amethyst cluster, budding amethyst 1.

page.title: How It Grows
text: A crop grows on random ticks (and a sprinkler's) at full pace while every factor is ideal, at half pace while some are only tolerable, and not at all while one is outside its range. Look at it (or use it with an empty hand) to see which.

page.title: Four Crops
text:
- Sunpetal: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 11 (best 13+); nutrients at least 1 (best 3+); diversity at least 1 (best 3+); disturbance at most 5 (best up to 2). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.
- Dewmoss: moisture at least 5 (best 7+); light at most 12 (best up to 9); nutrients at least 1 (best 2+). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.
- Gloamcap: moisture at least 2 (best 3+); light at most 9 (best up to 6); nutrients at least 2 (best 4+); disturbance at least 1 (best 3+), at most 15 (best up to 10). It costs 2 nutrients a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.
- Mendvetch: moisture at least 1 (best 3+); light at least 8 (best 11+); disturbance at most 6 (best up to 3). It gives 1 a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.

page.title: Harvest
text: A ripe crop (step 3) is harvested with an empty hand, or by a Gleaner: its produce and Verdant Chaff, and it falls back to step 1 to grow again. A Mendvetch next to other crops also speeds them, as legumes do.

page.title: Sunpetal
text: Your first Sunpetal comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Recipe: jugcraft:sunpetal. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Dewmoss
text: Your first Dewmoss comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Recipe: jugcraft:dewmoss. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Gloamcap
text: Your first Gloamcap comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Recipe: jugcraft:gloamcap. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Mendvetch
text: Your first Mendvetch comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Recipe: jugcraft:mendvetch. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Verdant Heart
text: Set on a bed, it beats every 10 seconds: in its niche it spends 1 nutrient and makes 2 Verdance (1 while a factor is merely tolerable), up to 64. Beside a Ley Pylon it pours in, 3 Verdance for 2 Ley Charge. Its niche: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 8 (best 12+); nutrients at least 1 (best 4+); diversity at least 2 (best 3+); disturbance at most 10 (best up to 6).
Recipe: jugcraft:verdant_heart. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Mulch Maw
text: Feed it plant matter (by hand or hopper): seeds, leaves and the crops are a quarter of a nutrient, chaff, vines and cane a half, fruit and roots three quarters, bread and hay a whole one. Every 2 seconds it eats one and, for every 4 quarters, gives a nutrient to the poorest bed within 3 blocks. Nothing composted gives back what it cost to grow.
Recipe: jugcraft:mulch_maw. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Habitat Gauge
text: Set on a bed, it reads the habitat there as a comparator signal: use it with an empty hand to choose a factor, or use a crop on it to read how well that crop would grow (15 thriving, 8 slowly, 0 not at all).
Recipe: jugcraft:habitat_gauge. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Gleaner
text: Harvests ripe crops within 3 blocks into its 9 slots (hoppers take them out), 1 Verdance a harvest, drawn from a Verdant Heart within 4 blocks.
Recipe: jugcraft:gleaner. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Celestial Attunement
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at the instruments that measure the sky. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Spyglass
- Clock
- Compass
- Phantom Membrane
- Glow Ink Sac

page.title: Observed
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: Your touch now aligns an Orrery Observatory, and an Astrolabe answers you. To master Celestial Attunement, observe 3 different patterns through an observatory (use it with an empty hand while one is up).

page.title: Mastered
text: You can recall a pattern you have seen when the sky is empty.

page.title: The World's Clock
text: The sky keeps the world's own clock, the one the sun and moon follow: a day is 20 minutes, night runs from 19:00 to 05:00, and the moon goes from full to new and back every 8 days. Every player sees the same sky, and so does the world after a restart. What your screen draws (a shader's moon, your render settings) never changes what is up.

page.title: The Patterns
text:
- The Full Moon: on the full moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, a clear sky. Pays 4 resonance; Moonsight: you see in the dark while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.
- The New Moon: on the new moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 4 resonance; Spring Tide: you breathe under water while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.
- The Lantern Star: every 3 days (days that leave 1 over 3), 18:00 to 20:00, a clear sky. Pays 2 resonance; Lantern Hands: you dig and work faster while it is up. Attuning costs 2, recalling 6.
- The Echo Comet: every 19 days (days that leave 7 over 19), 20:00 to 04:00, a clear sky. Pays 8 resonance; Comet's Wake: you run faster while it is up. Attuning costs 6, recalling 16.
- The Winter Crown: every 2 days (days that leave 1 over 2), in winter, 21:00 to 03:00, a clear sky. Pays 3 resonance; Frostmantle: fire does not burn you while it is up. Attuning costs 3, recalling 9.
- The Harvest Moon: every night, in the Harvest Moon, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 6 resonance; Feast Favour: villagers trade with you as with a hero while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.

page.title: The Forecast
text: Use an Orrery Observatory with an empty hand, or ask with /jugcraft concordance sky, to read the forecast: today's day, time, moon and season, and every pattern up now or rising in the next 8 days, with when it rises, the weather it needs and the time of year it keeps to.

page.title: Seasons
text: Some patterns keep to a time of year. The Winter Crown comes round only in Jugcraft's winter (the server's date; with seasons off, all year). The Harvest Moon pattern is the Halloween event's own Harvest Moon: it rises on the nights the event says, and never outside them.

page.title: Orrery Observatory
text: Set it under the open sky in the Overworld. Placed by a Starwatcher it is aligned to them; otherwise a Starwatcher's empty hand aligns it. Every 5 seconds it looks up: from each pattern up and in view it gathers that pattern's resonance, up to 32.
Recipe: jugcraft:observatory. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Once Each Time
text: Each time a pattern comes round it pays its keeper once, however many observatories they keep. Turning the world's clock back brings back only nights that have paid; turning it forward cannot pay sooner than half the pattern's period of real play. Its keeper's party may draw its resonance into an astrolabe (use the astrolabe on it).

page.title: Why It Waits
text: It says why it is idle: nothing up, unaligned, clouded over (for a pattern that needs a clear sky), something hiding the sky, not in the Overworld, full, already gathered, or too soon.

page.title: Astrolabe
text: It holds up to 32 resonance. Use it where you can see a risen pattern: it spends the pattern's cost and attunes you to it, and its effect is yours while the pattern stays up (at most 8 minutes; use it again to renew). Death ends an attunement.
Recipe: jugcraft:astrolabe. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Recall
text: A master may attune when nothing is up, by recalling the pattern they last observed: it costs the pattern's recall price and lasts 2 minutes, once each time the pattern comes round. Stored resonance is the alternative to waiting, never a way round the sky's count.

page.title: Crimson Rites
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at living things that bleed or sting. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Sweet Berries
- Crimson Roots
- Crimson Fungus
- Nether Wart
- Spider Eye

page.title: Observed
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: The Crimson Chalice answers you now. To master Crimson Rites, grow a Thornheart Blade you wield to its second stage.

page.title: Mastered
text: You know what a life can give, and what it cannot.

page.title: Crimson Chalice
text: Use it to make an offering: 4 health for up to 4 Vitae, which the chalice holds (up to 32). An offering never leaves you below 8 health, never comes within 5 seconds of the last, and takes no health when the chalice is full.
Recipe: jugcraft:crimson_chalice. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Three Things Apart
text: Health is yours to heal as ever. Vitae is what an offering made of it. Exhaustion is what offering leaves behind: each offering adds 3 points, and they clear one every 2 minutes and by nothing else: no food, potion, spell or regeneration. Healing to full does not let you offer again as if fresh.

page.title: Efficiency
text: An offering's yield falls with your exhaustion: 0 to 3 points: 100%; 4 to 7 points: 50%; 8 to 11 points: 25%; at 12 no offering at all. Rounded down. So a careful offering now and then gives far more than many in a row. /jugcraft concordance vitae says all three, and how long until you are clear.

page.title: Crimson Surge
text: Sneak and use the chalice: 6 Vitae become 6 Focus at once, at most once a minute and never beyond your full Focus. An emergency measure: what you can offer in an hour is bounded by your exhaustion, so it never becomes a spring of Focus.

page.title: Thornheart Blade
text: A living sword. It grows by three kinds of deed: slaying hostile creatures, enduring harm while you wield it, and being nourished (use the chalice with the blade in your other hand: 2 Vitae for 8 vigor).
Recipe: jugcraft:thornheart_blade. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Varied Use
text: Each deed pays by how often its kind of creature or harm has come up today: 4, 2, 1, 1, then nothing; each kind of deed pays at most 24 a day. A mob farm or a cactus stops paying at once. Its stages need several kinds: Awakened (20, two kinds with 5), Grown (60, every kind with 10), Flourishing (150, every kind with 30).

page.title: Vigor
text: Each stage adds 1 attack damage while the blade has vigor; every blow on a living creature spends 1. Without vigor its powers sleep, but nothing it has grown is lost.

page.title: Binding Arts
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at what binds one thing to another. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Lead
- Name Tag
- Soul Lantern
- Saddle
- Echo Shard

page.title: Observed
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: A familiar, a spirit and a construct will answer you now. To master the Binding Arts, be served by each once: a familiar's mending, a spirit's delivery and a construct's trip.

page.title: Mastered
text: You keep many, and each keeps its own terms.

page.title: Bonding Charm
text: Use it to bind a Hearthling: one familiar a person. It keeps within 8 blocks of you and, when you are badly hurt, mends you. Use the charm again to call it to your side; sneak to release it.
Recipe: jugcraft:bonding_charm. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: The Bond
text: The bond grows by time spent together, 1 a visit and at most 24 a day, and fades by 4 for each day you are online but away from it. At 20 it mends you (at most once a minute); at 60, twice as often. It never follows you into another dimension and never waits in a place that is not loaded: it simply waits where it is.

page.title: Spirit Anchor
text: Use it to seal an agreement with a Gathering Shade, recorded as a Bound Will: it gathers dropped items within 8 blocks of the anchor, from 19:00 to 05:00, at most 64 times a day, carrying 16 at a time, and brings them to the anchor (hoppers below take them out).
Recipe: jugcraft:spirit_anchor. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Its Terms
text: Outside its hours, its area or its work it waits at the anchor and says so; when its day's work is done it is finished until tomorrow. It never takes what you could not take yourself (a protected town). Sneak and use the anchor to suspend or resume it; break the anchor to release it: it leaves what it carried and departs.

page.title: Clockwork Porter
text: Unfold it on a block. Use a Porter Key on two containers (its source and its target), then on the porter. It carries 16 items a trip, spends 2 Ley Charge a trip (it holds 64, drawn from a Ley Pylon by its source that you may use) and wears 1 of its 64 integrity; each copper ingot mends 16.
Recipe: jugcraft:clockwork_porter. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Porter Key
text: Sets a porter's route.
Recipe: jugcraft:porter_key. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Why It Waits
text:
Look at a worker (Jade), use it with an empty hand, or ask /jugcraft concordance workers (which also lists workers that are not loaded, with what they last said):
- following: following its person
- supporting: mending its person
- travelling: on its way
- working: working
- returning: taking what it carries home
- idle: idle: nothing to do
- waiting for resources: waiting for resources (its source is empty or gone)
- blocked by access: blocked: its keeper may not take from or give to that place
- cannot navigate: cannot find a way there
- outside agreement: outside its agreement (the hours, the area or the work)
- finished: finished: its work for the day is done
- owner offline: waiting: its person is not here
- other dimension: waiting: its person or route is in another dimension
- destination unloaded: waiting: its destination is not loaded
- suspended: suspended by its holder
- needs repair: needs repair (copper)
- no energy: out of Ley Charge (a pylon by its source fuels it)
- full: full: there is no room to deliver
- disabled: switched off

page.title: Courier Post
text: Use the post with an item in your hand to request a stack of exactly that item (a named or enchanted one is not a plain one). Bind a Porter Key to the post, then use the key on a Clockwork Porter: it serves the post, fetching from containers within 8 blocks into the post's 9 slots (a hopper below takes them out).
Recipe: jugcraft:courier_post. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Accountable Transit
text: One courier takes a request at a time and reserves what it will carry, so two never reach for the same items. What a courier has picked up is held by the post's ledger, not by the courier: if it is broken, unloaded or the world restarts, its cargo waits at the post for another courier, or for you (/jugcraft concordance logistics recover). A full post keeps the rest in transit; a cancelled request, or one whose post is broken, takes its cargo back first.

page.title: Requests
text:
Use the post with an empty hand to read its last steps. /jugcraft concordance logistics lists your requests; request asks for a number of what you hold; cancel and recover take a request's number:
- open: waiting for a courier
- claimed: a courier is on it
- in transit: in transit
- stranded: stranded at the post (its courier is gone)
- returning: being taken back

page.title: Runesmithing
text:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at smithing stock. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Flint
- Gold Nugget
- Iron Nugget
- Lapis Lazuli
- Nether Quartz

page.title: Understood
text: Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes. To master Runesmithing, enhance rings in three different ways.

page.title: Artificer's Bench
text: Use it with ingots in hand to forge a Resonant Ring (8 Focus). Its quality and affixes are rolled once, on the server, and kept on the ring; you see them after they are made.
Recipe: jugcraft:artificer_bench. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Substrates
text:
- Copper: 4 ingot(s), capacity 4, 1 socket(s), 1 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2
- Iron: 4 ingot(s), capacity 5, 1 socket(s), 1 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2
- Gold: 4 ingot(s), capacity 7, 2 socket(s), 2 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2
- Netherite: 1 ingot(s), capacity 9, 3 socket(s), 2 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 0

page.title: Capacity
text: A ring's capacity is its substrate's, plus its quality (crude -1, sound 0, fine +1, masterwork +2), plus 1 while bonded. Affixes, runes and gems use it; nothing goes beyond it.

page.title: At the Bench
text: Hold the ring in your main hand and use the bench with, in your other hand: nothing (inspect it); redstone (reforge, 6 Focus); a rune's ingredient (inscribe, 4 Focus); a gem (socket); shears (unsocket the last gem); its substrate's ingot (repair); a lead (bond it to you, 10 Focus, or unbond it); flint (salvage, used twice to confirm).

page.title: What Each Keeps
text:
- Forge: a new ring: substrate, quality and affixes rolled once
- Reforge: keeps substrate, quality, runes, gems, bond and wear; new affixes
- Inscribe: keeps everything; adds a rune
- Socket: keeps everything; sets a gem
- Unsocket: keeps everything but the last gem, which comes back whole
- Bond: keeps everything; the ring serves only you, with one more capacity
- Unbond: keeps everything but the bond
- Repair: keeps everything; mends wear
- Salvage: gives back some substrate and every gem; destroys quality, affixes, runes and bond

page.title: Gems
text:
- Amethyst (amethyst shard): capacity 2
- Emerald (emerald): capacity 1
- Diamond (diamond): capacity 2
- Lapis (lapis lazuli): capacity 1
- Quartz (quartz): capacity 1

page.title: Runes
text:
- Rune of Radiance (glowstone dust): capacity 2
- Rune of Swiftness (sugar): capacity 2
- Rune of Warding (obsidian): capacity 3
- Rune of Vigor (golden carrot): capacity 2

page.title: Wearing
text: Wear the ring in a ring slot. It wears one point every 30 seconds worn; at its last point it is dull and gives nothing until repaired, but it never breaks. A bonded ring serves only its bond.

page.title: Relic Lore
text:
Once you understand First Light, examine something that has outlived its maker (sneak and use):
- Heart of the Sea
- Nautilus Shell
- Totem of Undying
- Eye of Ender
- Recovery Compass
Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Relic Lore.

page.title: Where Relics Work
text:
A relic works only where it is meant to: held in a particular hand, worn in an armour slot or an accessory (Trinkets) slot, or installed in a Reliquary Shrine. Each relic names its places.
Anywhere else it does nothing: carried loose in your inventory, worn for show in a cosmetic slot, held in the other hand, or kept in a chest, a shulker box or a bundle (nothing inside those is ever looked at).
/jugcraft concordance relics lists the relics you carry, where each one is, and whether it works or exactly why not.

page.title: Wardlight Lantern
text:
Holds 64 charge.
- held in the off hand: glowing on hostile creatures within 12 blocks for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse
- installed in a Reliquary Shrine: glowing on hostile creatures within 24 blocks for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why
Recipe: jugcraft:wardlight. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Hearthstone
text:
Holds 48 charge.
- worn in an accessory slot: regeneration on you for 5 s, every 10 s, 2 charge a pulse; needs ten calm seconds, someone hurt
- installed in a Reliquary Shrine: regeneration on your party within 8 blocks for 5 s, every 10 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs someone hurt
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why
- binds to the first player it serves, and then serves only them
Recipe: jugcraft:hearthstone. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Stormglass Orb
text:
Holds 32 charge.
- held in the main hand: speed on you for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs the open sky above
- cannot be installed
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why
Recipe: jugcraft:stormglass. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Owlsight Circlet
text:
Holds 32 charge.
- worn on the head: night vision on you for 22 s, every 10 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs the dark of night
- cannot be installed
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why
Recipe: jugcraft:owlsight_circlet. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Reliquary Shrine
text: Use a relic on an empty shrine to install it, if it has an installed way of working. Use any other relic on it (or one that cannot be installed) to recharge it: each Ley Charge from the Ley Pylons within 2 blocks gives 4 charge. An installed relic is charged from those pylons as it works, 8 a second. Use the shrine with an empty hand to take its relic back. Only its owner and their party may use it.
Recipe: jugcraft:reliquary_shrine. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Many Relics
text: However many relics you carry and wear, they pulse at most 2 times a second together; one owner's shrines, at most 4. A relic held back waits a second and is not spent. A relic spends charge only when its pulse changes something, and two relics giving the same effect never add up: the stronger holds.

page.title: Assay
text: Once you understand First Light, examine raw matter (sneak and use): raw iron, copper or gold, calcite or clay. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Assay.

page.title: Assayer's Scale
text: Use the scale with a material in your main hand to weigh it: its worth in grains of Prima Materia, what the stack would dissolve into, and what forming one costs. Use it again within ten seconds to dissolve the stack into your ledger. With an empty main hand and a material in your other hand, use it to form one more of it (the one you hold is the scale's pattern and is kept). Dissolving pays the exact worth of the whole stack rounded down; forming costs 5/4 of the worth rounded up, so every round trip loses. Your ledger holds at most 1,000,000 grains.
Recipe: jugcraft:assayers_scale. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: What Is Weighed
text: Only catalogued, plain materials. The scale refuses anything that holds other things, is named, written or marked, carries a creature or a block's state, has been changed in any other way, or carries magic: research, spells, relics, rings, living equipment, bound spirits. Owning something, or seeing it in a recipe book, never makes it weighable.

page.title: A Balanced Graph
text:
Every recipe between catalogued materials is declared, with the containers it gives back and its byproducts, and none may be worth more after than before. The scale's own dissolving and forming are part of the graph. /jugcraft concordance equivalence audit (operators) searches every cycle for a profitable one. Matter enters only from declared sources:
- cobblestone generator
- wheat farm
- oak tree
- sugar cane farm
- beehive

page.title: Sympathy
text: Once you understand First Light, examine a likeness (sneak and use): a fermented spider eye, a cobweb, a poisonous potato, a rabbit's foot, an armor stand. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Sympathy.

page.title: Taglocks and Links
text: Use a taglock on a creature to take a link to it. A fresh link has strength 100 and loses one every 12 s: it fades in twenty minutes. No link can be taken to yourself, to a player the server's rules do not let you harm (PvP off, or your party), or to anyone warded against linking. Every use checks the link again: its target must be in your dimension, within 128 blocks, and still yours to act against.
Recipe: jugcraft:taglock. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Curses
text:
Hold a linked taglock with a curse's reagent in your other hand and use it. A curse is bounded: a hindrance, never harm, for minutes, never forever. Each pulse is checked again: it skips while you are elsewhere or out of range or they are warded, and lifts for good if the rules stop letting you harm them.
- Curse of Lethargy: cobweb casts it; slowness for 10 s every 20 s, for 300 s in all; needs link strength 30 and 6 Focus; lifted by sugar
- Curse of Misfortune: rabbit foot casts it; unluck for 30 s every 30 s, for 600 s in all; needs link strength 20 and 4 Focus; lifted by amethyst shard
- Curse of Frailty: fermented spider eye casts it; weakness for 10 s every 20 s, for 300 s in all; needs link strength 40 and 8 Focus; lifted by blaze powder

page.title: Investigation and Remedies
text: Something weighs on you? Use a scrying glass (2 Focus a look). The first look names each curse and its remedy; the second names who cast it, unless they are warded against scrying. Hold the remedy in your other hand and use the glass to lift the curse (the remedy is spent). With a taglock in your other hand the glass reads its link. /jugcraft concordance hexes lists what you know. Anyone may use a scrying glass.
Recipe: jugcraft:scrying_glass. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Wards
text:
A ward sigil wards you against one kind of operation for twenty minutes (a fresh one renews it; wards never stack). Anyone may make and use one.
- Linking: no taglock can take a link to you (paper, dreamglass and string)
- Cursing: no curse pulse reaches you (paper, dreamglass and amethyst shard)
- Scrying: no scrying glass can name you as a caster, nor show where you are (paper, dreamglass and ink sac)
- Moving: no one else's Concordance effect can push you (paper, dreamglass and iron ingot)

page.title: Dreamwalking
text: Once you understand First Light, examine something from the edge of dreams (sneak and use): chorus fruit, an ender pearl, a white bed, a spore blossom. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Dreamwalking.

page.title: The Oneiric Censer
text: Use the censer at night (10 Focus) to dream. Everything you carry is held for you; you dream in adventure mode, with nothing, for at most 180 s, within 24 blocks of your body. Catch the dream wisps by walking into them: 3 gather at once and one more every 30 s; each is one dreamglass, at most 8. Use the censer again to wake.
Recipe: jugcraft:oneiric_censer. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Waking
text: However a dream ends, you wake with exactly what you carried, in the same slots, where your body lay, and never with more experience than you had (experience gained in the dream is gone; experience spent there, on an enchantment or a repair, stays spent). Anything you picked up while dreaming falls at your feet. You keep the dreamglass you caught; half if you strayed (left the dimension or went too far) or were hurt; none if you died (then your body dies with what it carried). Leaving the server mid-dream wakes you; a dream left open by a crash ends when you next join. Nothing worn in an accessory slot may come into a dream.

page.title: The Starbound Conclave
text: The Conclave is the fellowship of the Concordance's traditions, and its factions are those traditions: every research entry belongs to one. Once you understand First Light, use a Conclave Lectern (or /jugcraft concordance conclave join) to swear its oath. It replaces nothing: your party stays your party and Jugs stay the only coin. Renown is standing, never spent.

page.title: Renown
text: Renown comes from four kinds of work, each bounded so no one repeated deed can carry you: research (each state an entry reaches, once: 1, 2, 5, 10), commissions (each once a week, worth less each time, nothing after its third), teaching (someone advanced an entry by reading your notes: 3 renown, once per entry and learner, 4 per learner) and projects (each stage you helped, and the whole project, once).
Recipe: jugcraft:conclave_lectern. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Ranks
text:
A rank asks for renown, breadth and variety together.
- Aspirant: 0 renown, 0 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 0 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 1
- Fellow: 25 renown, 2 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 2 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 2; may begin projects
- Companion: 80 renown, 4 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 2 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects
- Luminary: 160 renown, 5 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 3 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects
- Starbound: 260 renown, 6 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 3 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects

page.title: Obligations
text: A member contributes something each week. A lapsed member keeps every point of renown but takes no tier II or III commission and begins no project until they contribute again; any contribution restores them. /jugcraft concordance conclave shows your standing, what the next rank needs and your obligation.

page.title: Commissions
text:
Hold what a commission asks for and use a lectern, or /jugcraft concordance conclave fulfil <commission>; practice commissions need only the practice carried through this week. /jugcraft concordance conclave commissions lists them and whether each is open to you.
- Oil for the Lamps (Lampwrights, tier 1): bring 16 glowstone dust; 4 renown, then 2, then 1; pays 2 amethyst shards
- The Seed Store (Greenwardens, tier 1): bring 32 wheat seeds; 4 renown, then 2, then 1; pays 2 emeralds
- Clean Vials (Alembists, tier 1): bring 12 glass bottles; 4 renown, then 2, then 1; pays 2 experience bottles
- The First Watch (Starwatchers, tier 1): an observation of the sky in the last week; 4 renown, then 2, then 1; pays 2 amethyst shards

page.title: Projects, Alone or Together
text: From Fellow, begin a project for yourself (/jugcraft concordance conclave project start <project> personal) or, as your party's leader, for your party (... party). Your own projects take only your work; your party's take any member's. Every stage that asks for several contributors also accepts the solo way: contributions on that many different days. Together a party finishes sooner, and every member who helped shares the achievement and the reward. Sneak and use a lectern with items to give them; use it with an empty hand to present what you understand; practices count by themselves. /jugcraft concordance conclave project shows progress anywhere.

page.title: Lecterns
text: A lectern serves the project of whoever placed it: their own, or (sneak and use it with an empty hand to switch) their party's. Anyone may swear the oath, see their standing and fulfil commissions at any lectern. Projects are kept by the world, not the lectern: breaking one loses nothing.

page.title: The Five Stages
text: The Concordance has five stages, each reached by any one of its routes once the stage before it is: they are the same stages as Jugcraft's (Discovery, Workshops, Specialization, Expeditions, Shared wonders). /jugcraft concordance stage shows yours and, for the next, every route and what it still needs.

page.title: Adept
