page.title: The Concord Spire
text: A Concord Spire is raised round a Spire Heart by a Master of the Concordance, and works only while it is kept: supplied every day, whole, and attended by keepers who go on practising its tradition. It is founded in one of three configurations, each with its own research, practice, crown, upkeep and field. A spire is the world's, not the heart's: breaking the heart, leaving or a restart loses nothing, and a heart put back where it stood answers again.

page.title: The Spire Heart
text: Place the heart where the spire will stand. Sneak and use it with an empty hand to choose a configuration (it says what each needs), then use it to found the spire. Afterwards an empty hand shows how it stands; its keeper sneaking shares it with their party or takes it back.
Recipe: jugcraft:spire_heart. See the Arcane Concordance codex for its live recipe view.

page.title: Raising It
text:
A spire is raised in four phases, in order:
1. Foundation: four Ley Pylons and four Warding Stones round the heart, as a Lesser Circle has them.
2. Shaft: three blocks of dark stone stacked on the heart, and the configuration's practice carried through twice.
3. Crown: the configuration's crown on the shaft, and the Kindling rite completed at a Lesser Circle within 12 blocks.
4. Kindling: the spire's upkeep held three days in a row.

page.title: The Kindling
text:
The Crown is finished by the Kindling, a ritual at a Lesser Circle within 12 blocks of the heart, taught by Circle Lore: Kindles a Concord Spire within 12 blocks whose crown stands: each participant is shielded for two minutes, and the spire's Crown is finished.

Offer: 8 Glowstone Dust, 2 Gold Ingot, 1 Ender Pearl.
Takes: one practitioner, 8 Focus each, 6 steps (12 seconds), drawing 2 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (48 in all).

page.title: Lantern Spire
text:
Needs: First Light mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers complete rituals.
Crown: lumen sconce over glowstone.
Upkeep a day: 4 glowstone dust and 8 Ley Charge.
Its field kindles light in the dark open air within 24 blocks, so nothing hostile spawns there, at most 4 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

page.title: Verdant Spire
text:
Needs: Verdant Husbandry mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers tend living devices.
Crown: flowering azalea over moss block.
Upkeep a day: 8 bone meal and 6 Ley Charge.
Its field grows the crops within 16 blocks a step at a time, at most 6 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

page.title: Star Spire
text:
Needs: Celestial Attunement mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers observe the sky.
Crown: lightning rod over amethyst block.
Upkeep a day: 2 glow ink sacs and 8 Ley Charge.
Its field restores Focus to its keepers within 24 blocks and reveals hostile creatures there, at most 6 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

page.title: Realigning
text: /jugcraft concordance spire realign <configuration> changes the configuration of the spire you keep nearest you, if you know what the new one needs. Before the Crown nothing is lost; after it, the Foundation and the Shaft stand, and the new crown, its Kindling and its days are done again.

page.title: Upkeep
text: From the Kindling on, each day the spire takes its configuration's item from the heart's store and Ley Charge from its own pylons. Put the item in by hand (use it on the heart), by hopper, or let a courier bring it: the heart files a request at a Courier Post within 16 blocks you may use whenever it holds less than two days' upkeep. A day without its upkeep takes nothing and the field rests until the next day that has it.

page.title: Attendance
text: A spire answers keepers who keep practising: its configuration's practice carried through by its keeper (or, if shared, their party) at least once every 7 days. Unattended, it rests; the next practice wakes it.

page.title: Damage and Repair
text: The heart checks every part of the spire it has raised. If one is missing or wrong, the spire rests and says which and where; put it back and it works again at once. Nothing is lost: not its phase, not its days. The spire never breaks or replaces a block itself: its light goes only into open air and its growth only into crops. A Verdant Bed's crop it hastens grows by its own rules: its bed pays at least a nutrient a step, and a Mendvetch fixes none while hastened.

page.title: Inspecting
text: Use the heart with an empty hand, or /jugcraft concordance spire, for its phase and what it still needs, its upkeep and store, its field and its attendance. Jade, when installed, shows the same at a glance. /jugcraft concordance spire abandon confirm forgets the spire you keep nearest you; what you built stays.

page.title: Hearthbinding
text:
Once you understand First Light, look at fire as the Hearthbinders do: something kept and used, never let loose. Sneak and use one of these to examine it:
- Coal
- Charcoal
- Torch
- Campfire
- Magma Block
- Blaze Powder
- Blaze Rod
- Magma Cream
- Fire Charge

page.title: Observed
text: You have examined 3 different things that hold fire. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench, or read someone's Research Notes.

page.title: Understood
text: You can now cast Hearthspark, Hearthguard and Cinderbolt with any Concordance instrument. To master Hearthbinding, kindle 3 different kinds of hearth with Hearthspark: a campfire, a soul campfire, a candle, a candle cake.

page.title: Mastered
text: You can now cast Hearthflare, and your Ember invocations cost a point less Focus.

page.title: Smoulder
text: A smouldering creature burns as anything on fire does, a point of damage a second, while the status lasts. Water and rain put it out; Fire Resistance and creatures born of fire ignore it; milk cures it. It never sets blocks alight.

page.title: Kindling
text: Hearthspark lights a hearth as flint and steel would, and only where you could light it by hand: claims, protected towns and spawn protection refuse it. It never places fire.

page.title: A Hearthbinder's Regalia
text: The Hearthbinders' gear gives fire Spell Power. Cinderbolt and Hearthflare add half a point of damage for each whole point of it: two points make one more. Wear a focus in the Spell Focus slot and a fire set as armour; the most is +6, so Cinderbolt deals 6 and Hearthflare 7. The Fire Bangle goes in a Bracelet slot. None of it holds Focus: Focus is yours alone.

text: A little knockback resistance. A fall that hurts you sends a wave through the ground: up to 12 hostile creatures within 3 blocks (more for a harder fall, at most 6) are harmed, thrown back and slowed. A few great foes, such as the Warden, take the harm but are neither thrown nor slowed.

page.title: The Journal
text: Press J (Controls: Concordance Journal) to open your journal. It shows what the server knows of your work: your Focus and stage, every research entry you have met and what its next state asks, each route to the next stage and what it still needs, and, once you know their traditions, your Vitae, the sky's forecast, your workers, deliveries, relics, the curses and wards on you, your Conclave standing, your spires and your Prima Materia.

page.title: Reading It
text: Each line says in words where you stand and what to do next. Exact values (in the journal, or in the Concordance settings) add the figures behind them: how many of what each way needs, limits and caps. The same reports print in chat with /jugcraft concordance status, stage, spire and the other Concordance commands.

page.title: Moving Around
text: Left, Right or the section buttons change section; Up, Down, Page Up and Page Down scroll; R asks for the journal again; X shows or hides exact values; Tab moves between buttons; Esc closes it. With GuiLib installed the journal opens as a full workspace; without it, or with Simple journal chosen in the settings, it opens as a plain screen showing the same.

page.title: Five Signs
text:
When something happens, the Concordance shows it where it happened, and only when it happened:
Preparation: glyphs drawn in, as a circle gathers.
Execution: light rising where work was done, or travelling along a real transfer: Ley Charge from a pylon to the circle it feeds, Radiance from a lantern into a pylon.
Success: a burst of light.

page.title: Two Warnings
text:
Shortage: grey smoke and sinking ash, with a hollow falling tone: something it needs is missing. A pylon short of charge, a missed upkeep, a formula without its ingredient, a worker that cannot go on.
Danger: flame and sparks thrown outwards, with a sharp rising warning: a circle's containment failing, a searing stir, a damaged spire.
Both sounds have subtitles.

page.title: Things As They Are
text: A crucible's liquid stands at its real volume, in the colour of its strongest property, muddied when it is murky. A searing crucible smokes and spits. A spire shows whether it is being raised, working, lacking or damaged. A worker that lacks something waits, tapping or looking about; one held up on its way stands still. A finished circle glows until its result is taken.

page.title: Visual Intensity
text: The Concordance settings choose how much is drawn: Full, Reduced or Minimal (warnings only). Large workshops draw no more than a set amount each moment, and warnings are never hidden. Reduced motion keeps everything calmer.
